title: You & Me
coreMove: Identify your own game before copying someone else's signal.
sourcePressure: Financial behavior can be rational for one horizon and costly for another; advice travels badly across different incentives.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Assuming one smart person's move is automatically transferable.

hook: opening with a generic paycheck scene
opening with a moral lesson about discipline
opening You & Me with a swapped-in personal finance anecdote
counterintuition: reducing You & Me to common-sense advice
tryThisNow: write down your values for ninety seconds
asking for a generic money reflection instead of the different game move
examples: reusing visible anchors from adjacent chapters instead of different game and horizon

exampleSpecs.domain: a long-term saver ignoring a day trader's urgent alert in a group chat
exampleSpecs.audience: an investor whose horizon differs from the loudest voice
exampleSpecs.stakes: copying the trade converts someone else's game into his risk
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he writes his holding period above the alert before deciding whether it applies
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a phone buzzing with a trade alert beside a retirement account screen

exampleSpecs.domain: a landlord misreading a developer's cash offer as proof the neighborhood is doomed
exampleSpecs.audience: a property owner separating another player's incentives from her own needs
exampleSpecs.stakes: selling in panic may solve the developer's timeline, not hers
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she asks what deadline the buyer faces before treating the offer as information
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a purchase offer slid under a rowhouse door

exampleSpecs.domain: a nonprofit treasurer resisting advice from a tech CFO about cash reserves
exampleSpecs.audience: a treasurer with donor restrictions and payroll obligations unlike a startup
exampleSpecs.stakes: borrowing the CFO's urgency could endanger restricted funds
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she marks which dollars are restricted before applying any outside cash rule
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a grant ledger with colored tabs for restricted funds

exampleSpecs.domain: a retiree filtering financial television through her own income needs
exampleSpecs.audience: a retiree who must distinguish entertainment urgency from spending horizon
exampleSpecs.stakes: acting on someone else's segment could create real bill risk
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she writes next year's withdrawals on the notepad before the host's prediction matters
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a muted financial channel above a handwritten withdrawal schedule

exampleSpecs.domain: a founder deciding whether to copy a competitor's cash-burning growth plan
exampleSpecs.audience: a founder whose capital stack and investors are different
exampleSpecs.stakes: copying the competitor may import their incentives without their funding
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: after a rival implodes, she compares investor terms rather than mocking the strategy
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a competitor press release beside her own investor term sheet

exampleSpecs.domain: a high school coach declining a training regimen borrowed from an elite academy
exampleSpecs.audience: a coach matching advice to players' bodies, schedules, and goals
exampleSpecs.stakes: copying the regimen could injure students with different constraints
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he maps academy practice hours against his players' bus schedules before adopting drills
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a practice plan next to an after-school bus timetable
